adoptionRule: No observation changes gameplay or development authority until an explicit human decision updates the owning authoritative document.

observations.idea: Immediate stabilization/jury-rigging precedes proper restoration.
observations.assessment: Supports combat Damage Control versus later Ship Repair; no extra repair layer.

observations.idea: Distributed repair stores improve immediate response.
observations.assessment: Repair Kits can abstract lockers; future maintainability could reflect distribution.

observations.idea: Computer casualties can be hardware or software/control failures.
observations.assessment: Future crossover; do not increase ordinary damage granularity.

observations.idea: Fire/atmosphere/propellant casualties can remain ongoing hazards until contained.
observations.assessment: Candidate bounded Hazard state; avoid room-level simulation.

observations.idea: Emergency isolation can sacrifice a local area to save the ship.
observations.assessment: Potential future command decision after Hazard/crew abstractions mature.

observations.idea: Damage Control work is itself hazardous.
observations.assessment: Supports future crew risk without current implementation.

observations.idea: Robots are well suited to vacuum/hazardous repair.
observations.assessment: Good human->automation->robotics progression.

observations.idea: Repairability can be designed into ship architecture.
observations.assessment: Strong maintainability tradeoff candidate.

observations.idea: Self-sealing/self-repairing materials provide qualitative progression.
observations.assessment: Strong later-TL lineage.

observations.idea: Compartmentation/fire-resistant construction limits damage propagation.
observations.assessment: Keep containment distinct from resistance, repair, and restoration.

observations.idea: Bomb-pumped lasers trade an expendable nuclear event for directed beam output.
observations.assessment: Potential sacrificial interceptor/Special Weapon rather than normal Main upgrade.

observations.idea: Nuclear reactor output can pump a laser directly.
observations.assessment: Strong fiction for selective reactor-enabling prerequisites.

observations.idea: Different pumping architectures trade geometry/materials/complexity differently.
observations.assessment: Supports architecture progression rather than one number ladder.

observations.idea: More extreme reactor states can unlock higher-output beam architectures.
observations.assessment: Reactor progress can expand the Energy design envelope.

observations.idea: Some high-output laser architectures may destroy their own active medium.
observations.assessment: Candidate architecture-specific destructive Forced Overload.

observations.idea: Thermal/material limits bound sustainable output.
observations.assessment: Use Strain/Overload abstraction instead of heat meter.

observations.idea: Waste heat remains an engineering cost.
observations.assessment: Rationale for existing currencies, not detailed thermal simulation.

observations.idea: Different nuclear-laser architectures operate at different wavelengths.
observations.assessment: Combine with wavelength-focused source before mechanics.

observations.idea: Extreme-duty active media may have unusual component resilience.
observations.assessment: Possible future trait; current damage model does not need it.

observations.idea: Shared high-temperature breakthroughs may cross reactor/propulsion/weapon categories.
observations.assessment: Possible enabling discovery; avoid blanket prerequisite chains.

observations.idea: Laser physical reach can exceed practical targeting/engagement capability.
observations.assessment: Strong support for physical range != attack eligibility.

observations.idea: Shorter wavelength concentrates a smaller spot at range.
observations.assessment: Potential range/focusing progression independent of damage.

observations.idea: High-frequency beams require increasingly specialized generation/focusing.
observations.assessment: Supports advanced branches/enabling technology.

observations.idea: Environment changes which wavelengths propagate well.
observations.assessment: Future atmospheric-combat relevance.

observations.idea: Microwave energy may fit electronics/EW roles better than thermal drilling.
observations.assessment: Potential electronic-attack/Special Weapon crossover.

observations.idea: Very high-frequency beams can create ionizing secondary effects.
observations.assessment: Do not translate directly into penetration values.

observations.idea: Fixed-frequency and tunable emitters create different operating choices.
observations.assessment: Strong adaptive-spectrum concept.

observations.idea: Free-electron lasers provide a broad tunable architecture.
observations.assessment: Strong long-term Energy branch candidate.

observations.idea: Frequency multiplication can be an enabling technology step.
observations.assessment: Useful lineage/flavor without current mechanics.

observations.idea: Precision beam effectiveness may depend strongly on tracking/jitter quality.
observations.assessment: Possible future family-specific degraded-fire/targeting interaction.

observations.idea: Fixed integration permits a larger weapon architecture than a turret.
observations.assessment: Supports large Main Weapon Space abstraction.

observations.idea: Longer acceleration structures can improve Kinetic/Particle velocity and range.
observations.assessment: Strong family-specific progression path.

observations.idea: Rigid mounting can improve pointing stability.
observations.assessment: Potential spinal accuracy/range identity.

observations.idea: Mount architecture reallocates structure between traverse/support and weapon/defense.
observations.assessment: Rationale for Space tradeoffs.

observations.idea: Whole-ship aiming becomes vulnerable to fast close targets.
observations.assessment: Natural long-range vs close-range counterplay.

observations.idea: Forward-fixed fire can conflict with major maneuver direction.
observations.assessment: Explore abstract alignment commitment before full facing.

observations.idea: Spinal weapons favor specialized siege/anti-capital roles.
observations.assessment: Fits generalized legal extreme-build philosophy.

observations.idea: Semi-fixed mounts can retain limited aim.
observations.assessment: Potential intermediate architecture.

observations.idea: Laser generators need not share Kinetic axial mount constraints.
observations.assessment: Guardrail against generic cross-family spinal bonuses.

observations.idea: Particle beams may permit limited steering despite axial accelerators.
observations.assessment: Potential distinct Particle identity.

observations.idea: Broadside fixed mounts decouple fire direction from thrust axis.
observations.assessment: Interesting only if facing/arcs earn their complexity.

observations.idea: Unguided Kinetic hit probability depends on projectile speed, range and target acceleration.
observations.assessment: Supports effective-range distinction.

observations.idea: Threatening Kinetic fire can force maneuver/evasion expenditure.
observations.assessment: Potential emergent suppression/evasion-pressure later.

observations.idea: Kinetic launcher architectures trade power, complexity, wear, timing and velocity differently.
observations.assessment: Strong non-linear Kinetic progression model.

observations.idea: Missiles are miniature spacecraft with modular propulsion/guidance/sensor/payload possibilities.
observations.assessment: Supports modular missile progression.

observations.idea: Missile size trades salvo density against individual seeker/payload/protection capability.
observations.assessment: Strong heavy-vs-saturation missile design axis.

observations.idea: A laser generator can route output through multiple beam directors.
observations.assessment: Energy-specific director architecture; no free extra attack packages.

observations.idea: Particle beams differ enough in propagation, impact and defenses to merit separate study.
observations.assessment: Serious future family candidate.

observations.idea: Macron accelerators produce dense microscopic high-velocity projectile streams.
observations.assessment: Potential late accelerator branch.

observations.idea: Plausible plasma weapons often converge toward particle/direct-energy behavior.
observations.assessment: Do not add Plasma by genre convention alone.

observations.idea: PDS can branch into Kinetic/flak, laser and interceptor-missile architectures.
observations.assessment: Strong future branching direction.

observations.idea: PDS may use local sensing/control and ship-level information together.
observations.assessment: Strong support for current local PDS architecture.

observations.idea: Active emitters can be targeted by anti-radiation/home-on-emission weapons.
observations.assessment: Elegant future counterplay to strong active emissions.

observations.idea: EW includes deception/false signatures/comms disruption, not only raw jamming.
observations.assessment: Strong qualitative EW progression.

observations.idea: Space mines make most sense near strategic constraints; mobile/ranged mines blur toward missiles/platforms.
observations.assessment: Prefer system/chokepoint hazards over generic tactical mine spam.

observations.idea: Turrets include substantial internal support/feed/traverse architecture.
observations.assessment: Reinforces current Space abstraction.

observations.idea: Radiation can create crew/electronics effects distinct from hull damage.
observations.assessment: Wait for dedicated radiation source and mature crew/internal systems.

observations.idea: Effective engagement range emerges from weapon physics, tracking, target mobility, guidance, EW and defenses.
observations.assessment: Strong cross-system confirmation of current architecture.

observations.idea: Scientific categories blur; gameplay families should be based on coherent lineage/behavior.
observations.assessment: Use gameplay identity rather than taxonomy purity.

observations.idea: Exceptional weapons are memorable when firing requires buildup/commitment/consequence.
observations.assessment: Strong principle for rare/Precursor/experimental systems.

observations.idea: Long-duration zero-g causes health effects not fully solved by exercise.
observations.assessment: Star Cluster eventually needs a deliberate long-duration gravity answer.

observations.idea: Artificial gravity can come from generated fields, linear acceleration or rotation.
observations.assessment: Foundational setting choice remains open.

observations.idea: Small centrifuges require higher spin rates and harsher Coriolis/gradient conditions.
observations.assessment: Model quality/architecture, not RPM equations.

observations.idea: Large rings suit stations/civilian habitats better than compact warships.
observations.assessment: Strong role/visual differentiation.

observations.idea: Deployable/folding centrifuges suggest cruise versus combat configurations.
observations.assessment: Good warship fiction; mechanize only if preparedness gameplay earns it.

observations.idea: Rotating joints create power/fluid transfer and maintenance complexity.
observations.assessment: Rationale for architecture cost without component-level detail.

observations.idea: Spin sections exchange angular momentum and create gyroscopic effects.
observations.assessment: Keep as fiction; no gyro dynamics simulator.

observations.idea: Whole-ship/tethered rotation offers alternative artificial-gravity layouts.
observations.assessment: Useful exploration/emergency flavor.

observations.idea: Hub docking is naturally easier than rim docking on a rotating habitat.
observations.assessment: Good station-layout logic without docking minigame.

observations.idea: Generated gravity can distinguish later technological generations from spin gravity.
observations.assessment: Strong design-envelope breakthrough candidate; preserve legacy spin usefulness.

observations.idea: Kinetic and Energy weapon families can differ in resource burden: finite ammunition and magazines versus power/thermal demand, with hybrid technologies sometimes carrying both.
observations.assessment: Useful family identity axis; do not turn it into an absolute physics taxonomy.

observations.idea: Kinetic systems can vary through projectile, accelerator and ammunition changes, while Energy systems can vary through emitter, focusing, steering and efficiency changes.
observations.assessment: Strong support for asymmetric family-specific TL progression.

observations.idea: Radiation-oriented weapons can be countered by dedicated shielding/hardening, but that protection carries engineering cost.
observations.assessment: Prefer specialist hardening/traits over a universal radiation-resistance stat until radiation mechanics earn that complexity.

observations.idea: Particle composition and mass can change how deeply energy is deposited and how strongly secondary ionizing effects threaten crew/electronics.
observations.assessment: Potential future specialization axis; avoid detailed dose simulation.

observations.idea: Radiological contamination and lingering exposure can matter after an attack even when the immediate structural effect is limited.
observations.assessment: Better suited to scenario/salvage consequences than universal tactical bookkeeping.

observations.idea: Minefields derive much of their value from uncertainty and area denial rather than raw damage alone.
observations.assessment: Supports observer-safe hazard regions and route pressure rather than visible mine-counter spam.

observations.idea: Mine counterplay can include sensing, probes, spoofing, sweeping, disposable clearing assets and route choice.
observations.assessment: Strong counterplay vocabulary if minefields are introduced.

observations.idea: As mines gain range, mobility or autonomous pursuit they increasingly blur into disposable platforms or missiles.
observations.assessment: Classify future systems by behavior rather than naming convention.

observations.idea: Large weapon mounts trade structural mass/output against tracking responsiveness and target-switch agility.
observations.assessment: Useful distinction for heavy/spinal/turreted architectures without degrees-per-second simulation.

observations.idea: Phased-array or other nonmechanical beam steering can improve rapid retargeting and distributed aperture use without increasing total generator output.
observations.assessment: Strong high-TL integration direction; no free extra attack packages.

observations.idea: Kinetic ammunition can use penetrators, proximity/submunition packages, guided or smart projectiles, specialized armatures and exotic materials in addition to changes in the launcher itself.
observations.assessment: One of the richest Kinetic progression axes.

observations.idea: Rail, coil and hybrid/helical electromagnetic launchers trade timing/control complexity, current, wear, projectile interaction and accelerator architecture in different ways.
observations.assessment: Promising maturation branch; exact implementation remains open.

observations.idea: Advanced laser systems can distribute generation and steering across multiple apertures/arrays for resilience and rapid engagement changes.
observations.assessment: Corroborates distributed-director architecture while keeping one bounded output pool.

observations.idea: Laser-coupled particle concepts offer an exotic route to reduced divergence or extreme-range directed effects.
observations.assessment: Preserve as exotic/Precursor/high-TL inspiration rather than ordinary progression.

observations.idea: Physical/active decoys are a distinct EW tool from continuous jamming and can attack seeker discrimination rather than raw signal strength.
observations.assessment: Potential qualitative EW progression without another stacked rating.

observations.idea: Communications jamming can attack command links and datalinks rather than only sensor discrimination.
observations.assessment: Especially relevant to command-guided missile chains; needs explicit observer-safe mechanics later.

observations.idea: Directional jamming can concentrate effect when threat direction is known, at the cost of coverage/flexibility.
observations.assessment: Interesting specialist system; avoid baseline facing/allocation micromanagement.

observations.idea: Point-defense systems can use high-volume kinetic fire, proximity/submunition packages, local fire-control improvements and guided intercept rounds.
observations.assessment: Strong family-specific PDS progression vocabulary.

observations.idea: Point defense operates during a short terminal closing interval in which reaction time and opportunities to re-engage an incoming threat are limited.
observations.assessment: Supports current abstraction; no need for turret-arc or burst-by-burst timing.

observations.idea: Anti-missile missiles form a distinct guided defensive layer with finite interceptor inventory and potentially longer reach than terminal gun/laser PDS.
observations.assessment: Natural future extended-defense family; keep distinct from standard terminal PDS.

observations.idea: Destroying or mission-killing an incoming missile can still leave high-velocity fragments that are physically hazardous.
observations.assessment: Record the physical caveat, but retain Star Cluster's attack-package abstraction and no universal residual-debris damage roll unless a special trait later earns one.

observations.idea: Macron weapons fire enormous streams of microscopic projectiles that can be carried in very large physical quantities, while their electrostatic accelerator infrastructure can be substantial.
observations.assessment: Distinctive late-Kinetic trade: abundant attack material, demanding launcher.

observations.idea: Fissile or fusion payloads inside macrons can release additional nuclear energy on impact, and related microreaction concepts can also be used for power generation or propulsion.
observations.assessment: Excellent example of enabling science shared across categories without merging ownership.

observations.idea: Particle species can shift a beam from shallow material damage toward deeper ionization/radiation and electronics effects.
observations.assessment: Strong subtype/progression axis; does not require a universal radiation bar.

observations.idea: Neutralizing a charged particle beam after acceleration can reduce electrostatic bloom and preserve a tighter beam over distance.
observations.assessment: Strong qualitative maturation step.

observations.idea: Electrostatic, magnetic and plasma-screen defenses provide specialist countermeasure concepts against particle beams.
observations.assessment: Prefer specialist auxiliaries/traits over redefining ordinary shields.

observations.idea: Ultra-relativistic electron beams greatly reduce bloom, carry extreme energy, penetrate strongly, generate high-energy secondary radiation and are very difficult to deflect.
observations.assessment: Preserve as exceptional/Precursor/very-late candidate unless substantial costs and counters are proven.

observations.idea: Continuous-wave and pulsed lasers deposit energy differently; short high-energy pulses can create mechanical shock and drilling-like effects, and pulse duration changes the result.
observations.assessment: Strong basis for a pulsed-laser maturation step; exact DAM/APEN/mode mechanics remain open.

observations.idea: Chemical lasers can trade finite expendable reactants for high output/reduced ship electrical dependence.
observations.assessment: Useful faction/specialist Beam identity; Beam does not have to mean infinite electrical ammunition.

observations.idea: Distributed strategic focusing arrays can create system-scale laser infrastructure useful for weapons, propulsion, sensing, communications or power transfer.
observations.assessment: Better fit for installations/Precursor infrastructure than ordinary cruiser Main Weapons.

observations.idea: Superweapon status is a role/scale/narrative descriptor, and extraordinary effects can emerge from unusual uses of established systems rather than a dedicated weapon family.
observations.assessment: Do not create a Superweapon TL family; use rare scenario/Precursor/artifact effects when appropriate.

observations.idea: Nuclear devices are commonly missile-delivered, and nuclear energy can also be engineered into several directed terminal effects rather than only an omnidirectional detonation.
observations.assessment: Strong support for separating missile delivery/guidance from warhead effect.

observations.idea: Bomb-pumped beams, directed plasma charges and nuclear formed penetrators can focus nuclear output into qualitatively different terminal attack mechanisms.
observations.assessment: Rich advanced-warhead vocabulary; exact Star Cluster stats remain open.

observations.idea: The same directed nuclear-energy principles can be applied to propulsion or converted back into weapons such as plasma jets and explosively formed penetrators.
observations.assessment: Use causal prerequisite tags if adopted; do not merge the research families.

observations.idea: Enhanced-radiation nuclear devices deliberately shift more of their output toward neutrons, threatening crew over distances where strong material damage may be much lower.
observations.assessment: Potential niche payload after crew/internal systems mature; specialist hardening can counter it.

observations.idea: A deliberately broader, shorter-ranged directed nuclear effect can be used defensively to destroy incoming weapons across a volume of space.
observations.assessment: Interesting AMM/emergency-defense concept with obvious scarcity/collateral costs.

observations.idea: Missile designs vary separately in propulsion/endurance, guidance and sensors, warhead type, physical size and launcher integration.
observations.assessment: Strong structural support for modular missile progression.

observations.idea: Unguided rockets/torpedoes remain a legitimate distinct munition form with shorter useful reach but lower guidance complexity.
observations.assessment: Supports retaining unguided rockets as a real capability combination.

observations.idea: Seeker sophistication and countermeasures form an arms race in discrimination, decoys/blinding and onboard power/integration complexity.
observations.assessment: Higher-TL guidance can improve robustness/information quality rather than raw warhead damage.

observations.idea: Many-small versus few-large missile designs trade defensive saturation against per-vehicle sensor, power, protection and payload capability.
observations.assessment: Maps naturally to different physical compositions inside one Missile Flight abstraction.

observations.idea: Missile engine/propellant choices trade acceleration, range/endurance and cost; beamed-power propulsion can extend range while shifting the propulsion power burden back to the launching platform.
observations.assessment: Useful progression axis; beamed-power missiles need a distinct reason to exist over firing the beam directly.

observations.idea: Projectile mass, velocity and construction can trade broad energy deposition against narrow penetration/internal effects.
observations.assessment: Supports family-appropriate DAM/APEN trade space without automatic penetration every TL.

observations.idea: Coilguns require precise staged electromagnetic timing, while railguns avoid that timing burden but face high-current, heating, arcing, erosion and materials problems.
observations.assessment: Good sparse cross-category prerequisite vocabulary.

observations.idea: Kinetic launchers can require recoil compensation, structural bracing, cooling and wear management in addition to the accelerator and projectile themselves.
observations.assessment: Strong abstraction support.

observations.idea: Proximity/submunition Kinetic packages can trade individual hit effect for a larger effective interception/damage volume, especially against exposed or small systems.
observations.assessment: Interesting ammunition specialization; avoid generic size accuracy modifiers.

observations.idea: Missile closing speed, maneuver and remaining propellant affect the terminal interception opportunity available to point defense.
observations.assessment: Useful rationale for bounded terminal-defense windows; defer detailed closing-time simulation.

observations.idea: Exploration is purposeful knowledge acquisition - mapping, resources, science and contact - rather than merely arriving first.
observations.assessment: Strong fit for Star Cluster exploration goals.

observations.idea: Sensors and disposable/reusable probes can automate tedious surveying while leaving the player to choose what merits investigation and risk.
observations.assessment: High-interest probe/survey direction; avoid repetitive manual scanning minigames.

observations.idea: Exploration ships benefit from endurance, ruggedness, efficiency, field repairability and carried spares because distant failures may be hard to fix.
observations.assessment: Strong support for self-sufficiency tradeoffs using existing repair/fuel systems.

observations.idea: Long expeditions are constrained by consumables and replenishment opportunities, and specialized harvesting equipment trades against carrying more supplies or better recycling.
observations.assessment: Model through broad resources/equipment choices rather than food/water calorie accounting.

observations.idea: Very advanced self-sufficiency technology can erase the feeling of distance unless failures or other constraints preserve meaningful expedition choices.
observations.assessment: Higher TL should reduce expedition problems without deleting the press-on/return-home tension.

observations.idea: Isolation from rescue and the possibility of being unable to return are core exploration hazards.
observations.assessment: Strong support for strandedness and return capability as campaign stakes.

observations.idea: Local resource gathering can extend an expedition, but extraction hardware competes with other ship capacity and may only be valuable in some failures/routes.
observations.assessment: Good optional expedition specialization; no large inventory taxonomy required.

observations.idea: Exploration is more memorable when discoveries have context and consequences rather than being interchangeable procedural scan targets.
observations.assessment: Use procedural generation to create distinct situations/decisions, not repetitive collection chores.

observations.idea: Passive sensing and active sensing provide different information and emission tradeoffs; even encrypted communications can reveal direction or activity.
observations.assessment: Strong support for separate active/passive behavior and observable emissions.

observations.idea: Different sensing modalities specialize in search, range, motion or identification rather than one sensor being best at everything.
observations.assessment: Useful rationale for abstract multimodal suites; do not expose six separate sensor-control panels.

observations.idea: Broad search/detection and precision fire-control tracking are distinct sensing tasks with different accuracy requirements.
observations.assessment: Strong support for search versus Firm weapons-quality track and Sensors versus Computing/Fire Control separation.

observations.idea: Redundant or multimodal sensing can preserve useful information when one channel is jammed, obscured or damaged.
observations.assessment: High-interest progression direction without simply raising sensor range.

observations.idea: Active fire-control illumination or other active sensing can warn the target that it is being observed or precisely tracked.
observations.assessment: Potential observer-safe warning information without exposing hidden enemy ratings.

observations.idea: Phased arrays and advanced processing can combine rapid steering, multiple tracks, communication/datalink and resistance to interference.
observations.assessment: Strong integrated-sensor maturation concept; keep player controls simple.

observations.idea: Friendly assets can share observations or hand off targeting information, making cooperative sensing a distinct capability from one sensor being stronger.
observations.assessment: High-interest networked-sensing candidate; preserve track provenance and information parity.

observations.idea: Exotic high-energy sensing channels can counter some low-observability techniques but require specialized emitters/detectors.
observations.assessment: Good alien/high-TL candidate, not an ordinary toggle.

observations.idea: Advanced sensing can require substantial computation for beam steering, noise filtering, detection tracking, track processing and signature recognition.
observations.assessment: Supports sparse causal cross-category requirements.

observations.idea: A precise positional/fire-control track need not imply complete identification of target class, equipment or intent.
observations.assessment: Useful information-control guardrail: Firm position can remain distinct from intelligence/identification.

observations.idea: Power-source suitability depends on mission, environment, scale, required output and operating duration rather than one universally superior generator.
observations.assessment: Supports overlapping technology generations and specialist sources.

observations.idea: Fission, fusion and antimatter systems carry different shielding, conversion, containment and integration burdens in addition to raw output.
observations.assessment: Useful family-specific progression vocabulary; avoid separate thermal/containment meters by default.

observations.idea: Power generation and energy storage solve different problems: sustained supply versus temporal mismatch and peak demand.
observations.assessment: High-interest distinction for batteries/capacitors and future power progression.

observations.idea: Storage technologies trade capacity, discharge rate, recharge, retention, footprint, cooling and reliability rather than scaling one capacity number.
observations.assessment: Strong qualitative storage progression axis.

observations.idea: Fusion power can convert fusion output through thermodynamic cycles or through more direct electrostatic/electromagnetic conversion methods.
observations.assessment: Good TL maturation concept without compulsory output inflation.

observations.idea: Antimatter offers very high energy release and can catalyze fission or fusion, but production, storage and powered containment are severe constraints.
observations.assessment: Interesting overlapping-generation path; exact Star Cluster TL mapping remains open.

observations.idea: Several power technologies can also be applied directly to propulsion, such as solar heating, nuclear thermal propulsion and fusion engines.
observations.assessment: Supports sparse cross-pollination rather than merging categories.

observations.idea: Solar, radioisotope and beamed-power systems can be useful specialist sources for probes, infrastructure or niche missions even when unsuitable as main combat reactors.
observations.assessment: Good worldbuilding/scenario technology; not every source needs a player-cruiser component.

observations.idea: Power systems can require substantial support infrastructure such as radiators, radiation shielding, containment, cryogenic cooling or structural reinforcement.
observations.assessment: Strong support for current abstraction philosophy.

observations.idea: Potential power and propulsion resources such as water, methane and fissile material can be found or processed from bodies within a solar system.
observations.assessment: Use broad compatible-resource/logistics abstractions if needed.

observations.idea: Stealth is reduced observability and uncertainty, not binary invisibility.
observations.assessment: Strong fit for graded observer information.

observations.idea: Low observability is sensor-specific; suppressing one signature channel does not automatically defeat every detection method.
observations.assessment: Avoid one universal stealth number if future mechanics need channel distinctions, but keep player controls simple.

observations.idea: Detection, identification and precise tracking are distinct mission-relevant information layers, and stealth can defeat any one of them without making the ship nonexistent.
observations.assessment: High-interest support for existing graded track architecture.

observations.idea: Thermal and propulsion emissions are difficult to hide; suppressing them tends to be temporary, costly or operationally constraining.
observations.assessment: Strong candidate for bounded quiet/thermal-suppression behavior, not a heat meter.

observations.idea: Ship actions such as hard burns, active sensing and other emissions can change observability over time.
observations.assessment: High-interest action-dependent signature direction.

observations.idea: Low-observable design can conflict with the ship's own sensing/emission needs; low-probability-of-intercept and advanced integration can mitigate that trade.
observations.assessment: Useful high-TL integration idea without guaranteeing perfect stealth.

observations.idea: Stealth and electronic warfare can reinforce each other but remain different tools: one reduces observability while the other interferes with information/discrimination.
observations.assessment: Preserve separate subsystem identities.

observations.idea: Passive low-observability design and active cloaking are distinct concepts with different costs and failure modes.
observations.assessment: If active cloak ever appears, treat it as a costly special system rather than Stealth +N.

observations.idea: All-angle observation in space makes perfect passive concealment difficult, especially for powered craft.
observations.assessment: Good guardrail against routine total invisibility.

observations.idea: Even suspected presence without exact position/identity can create tactical value, uncertainty and route pressure.
observations.assessment: Supports observer-safe suspected-contact states.

observations.idea: Biological and mechanical spacecraft form a continuum rather than mutually exclusive categories.
observations.assessment: Good taxonomy guardrail for alien generation.

observations.idea: Construction method, outward appearance and sentience/agency are independent design axes.
observations.assessment: Important: organic-looking need not mean living, and living need not look organic.

observations.idea: Biotechnology can be integrated throughout a vessel or localized to particular components/armor/control systems.
observations.assessment: Strong fit for biological alien components using existing compatibility/support-tag architecture.

observations.idea: Growth and regeneration are common biomechanical concepts but are not automatic properties of every living ship.
observations.assessment: Potential bounded self-healing branch; must be costed and explicitly present.

observations.idea: Living ships can relate to crew as passengers, hosts, symbionts, integrated pilots or control organisms.
observations.assessment: Rich narrative/boarding possibilities; no universal crew mechanic required.

observations.idea: Some biomechanical ship concepts depict the spacecraft itself as a sentient living being, in extreme cases treating the ship as equivalent to an entire civilization.
observations.assessment: High-interest narrative consequence for living alien ships.

observations.idea: Biomimetic visual design can be functional, purely stylistic or both; mechanical ships can use organic visual language without being biological.
observations.assessment: Useful procedural visual grammar; not a gameplay rule.

observations.idea: Repeated curves, ribs, spines, fins and subtly varying forms can create a coherent organic visual doctrine without copying a literal organism.
observations.assessment: Useful art/procedural-generation reference.

observations.idea: A spacecraft can look strongly mechanical while being living or sentient, while other designs can use biological-looking forms without being literal living organisms.
observations.assessment: Do not let organic/metallic art automatically reveal regeneration, sentience or other hidden mechanics.

observations.idea: Spacecraft must reject waste heat from power, electronics, crew and environment, making thermal management a foundational support requirement.
observations.assessment: Useful engineering basis for complete component footprint.

observations.idea: Spacecraft thermal-control systems can circulate coolant through heat exchangers and dedicated radiators to move internal waste heat to surfaces optimized for radiation.
observations.assessment: Strong support for hiding normal thermal support inside Space and operating characteristics.

observations.idea: Hotter/advanced radiators can reduce area and vulnerability but may demand more pumping power, materials capability or engineering complexity.
observations.assessment: Useful compactness-power-vulnerability tradeoff.

observations.idea: Thermal survivability can be improved through redundancy, protection, tougher construction or retractable radiators, each with costs.
observations.assessment: Good technology/race differentiation without universal exposed radiator hit locations.

observations.idea: Retracting radiators and relying on heat storage creates a temporary operating window before heat must be rejected again.
observations.assessment: High-interest thermal-suppression/protected-operation concept; prefer finite activations/duration/Strain over a heat bar.

observations.idea: Radiators deliberately emit thermal photons, and sufficiently high-temperature radiators can become visibly luminous as their emission spectrum shifts.
observations.assessment: Strong physical basis for qualitative action-dependent signature states.

observations.idea: Large radiator structures can be vulnerable in combat, motivating redundancy, protection, harder-to-damage designs or temporary retraction backed by heat storage.
observations.assessment: Potential effect through overload limits, Strain or reduced output rather than instant reactor explosion.

observations.idea: Solid, moving, droplet, membrane, magnetic and plasma radiator concepts provide multiple technological/alien expressions of the same support function.
observations.assessment: Use as race/technology flavor and bounded traits, not separate universal cooling rules.

observations.idea: Open-cycle cooling can handle exceptional thermal loads by consuming and discarding coolant rather than maintaining a closed loop.
observations.assessment: Possible finite-charge emergency/high-output auxiliary; do not add ordinary Coolant inventory by default.

observations.idea: Open-cycle cooling can be combined with closed-cycle radiators, using expendable coolant for unusually demanding thermal loads while radiators handle baseline continuous loads.
observations.assessment: Strong candidate for capability tags/support components rather than a sprawling research category.

observations.idea: FTL systems can be classified by travel topology - discontinuous versus continuous - and by constraints on entry, path and exit.
observations.assessment: Useful design-space taxonomy, not a replacement for current Star Cluster FTL.

observations.idea: FTL systems differ in whether transit requires fixed infrastructure or location-specific access, or can instead be initiated by a self-contained ship.
observations.assessment: Use FTL rules to preserve exploration geography and route choices.

observations.idea: Fixed gates, jump points and lanes naturally create chokepoints, shortcuts, crossroads and valuable locations.
observations.assessment: High-interest sector-population content layered on ordinary FTL.

observations.idea: Navigable hyperspace can use fixed-exit, fixed-direction or freely navigable travel rules, each allowing a different degree of control after entry.
observations.assessment: Useful progression vocabulary; do not replace current ladder without a dedicated design decision.

observations.idea: Infrastructure-based FTL and self-contained ship FTL can coexist in one setting; common traffic may rely on gates while more capable ships create their own access.
observations.assessment: Strong asymmetric civilization concept with explicit constraints.

observations.idea: Permanent FTL gateways or conduits can be natural or artificial and can act like fixed travel corridors between separated regions.
observations.assessment: Excellent Precursor/anomaly discovery type.

observations.idea: Navigable hyperspace can contain hazards, currents or navigation requirements.
observations.assessment: Represent at route/event level rather than building a second tactical map.

observations.idea: Some FTL environments depend on known routes, beacons or other navigation aids because travel away from them is dangerous.
observations.assessment: High-interest non-component exploration reward.

observations.idea: FTL access can be limited to particular locations, fixed routes, gateway devices or other entry conditions rather than being universally available everywhere.
observations.assessment: Preserve distance, strandedness and return-home decisions at high capability.

observations.idea: Object teleportation/portals are distinct capabilities from ordinary ship-scale interstellar FTL even when the fictional science overlaps.
observations.assessment: Keep separate so local logistics/boarding/tactical positioning are not accidentally erased.

observations.idea: The FTL taxonomy also includes distance shrinking, local or regional light-speed modification, backward time travel and reality/coordinate alteration as extreme mechanism classes.
observations.assessment: Excellent singular-artifact inspiration; do not normalize it into ordinary TL advancement.

observations.idea: FTL design should begin with explicit capabilities, limitations, costs and consequences; fictional mechanism can come later.
observations.assessment: Strong validation of Star Cluster's rules-first approach.

observations.idea: FTL rules shape travel time, information flow, trade, governance, warfare and strategic geography rather than merely setting a speed number.
observations.assessment: Useful world-generation lens; no immediate gameplay-rule change.

observations.idea: A good FTL limitation creates decisions, encounters or geography rather than mere procedural inconvenience.
observations.assessment: Evaluate each restriction by the gameplay opportunity it creates.

observations.idea: Slow/flexible onboard FTL can coexist with much faster fixed transit infrastructure, preserving exploration freedom while creating strategic routes.
observations.assessment: Very high-interest sector-generation pattern; ordinary Star Cluster FTL remains the reliable baseline.

observations.idea: Natural or artificial jump features become valuable content when they must be discovered, mapped, addressed, powered or otherwise understood.
observations.assessment: Excellent low-TL exploration opportunity through discovered routes.

observations.idea: A small set of explicit FTL rules can produce many downstream setting consequences, as shown by examples built around travel time, jump distance, fuel, gravity limits, addresses, power and gate access.
observations.assessment: Use two or three legible constraints rather than a large FTL simulation.

observations.idea: Rare exceptions to established FTL rules work best when they are explicit exceptional phenomena rather than casual inconsistencies.
observations.assessment: A Precursor gate/artifact may break one ordinary rule because the exception itself is content.

observations.idea: FTL can be disrupted or interdicted in some settings, creating strategic/scenario possibilities.
observations.assessment: Preserve as advanced/alien/installation possibility; avoid routine universal FTL-jammer stat contests.

observations.idea: FTL cost, maintenance, fuel, specialist personnel or political control can differentiate access and civilization reach.
observations.assessment: Useful faction/worldbuilding distinction without mandatory player bureaucracy.

observations.idea: FTL design can work forward from a chosen rule set or backward from the desired setting/story, and examining existing settings by reverse-engineering their rules can help.
observations.assessment: Mine the method, not Traveller/Stargate/Mass Effect numerical rules.

observations.idea: Whether faster-than-light communications exist is a separate rule from faster-than-light travel and strongly affects how quickly information, governance, trade and military reactions can spread.
observations.assessment: Useful strategic/worldbuilding axis to keep conceptually separate from ship travel; no Star Cluster rule change is made here.
